newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise as of Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise as of Jan 3.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of January 3 were $6.321 billion, compared to $6.313 billion on December 31.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of January 3 were $17.651 billion, compared to $17.509 billion as of December 31.
It said the increase of $8 million in international assets in the December 31-January 3 period was due to:
-- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $34 million;
-- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $1 million;

-- A net loss of $25 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base fell by 943 million pesos due to the seasonal demand for bills and coins.
The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank fell by 2.961 billion pesos, mainly as a result of greater expenditures than taxes collected.
Central bank credit to financial institutions fell by 4.686 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of the Treasury withdrawing funds.

* Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
